newsitem.title: FRANCE: Key Chirac fundraiser detained in French probe.
newsitem.headline: Key Chirac fundraiser detained in French probe.

text.p: A key fundraiser for President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party was detained by police at her home before dawn on Thursday and taken for questioning by a magistrate investigating suspected graft, justice sources said.

Louise-Yvonne Casetta, nicknamed "la cassette" (the safe) in the party because she was regarded as a major fundraiser, was picked up at six a.m. (0500 GMT) in an arrest technique usually reserved for suspects who police fear might flee.

The sources said she was expected to be placed under judicial investigation on suspicion of misuse of corporate funds in connection with a probe into alleged illicit funding of the RPR by the construction firm Maillard et Duclos in 1992-93.
Casetta was official head of personnel at the RPR until last September but she was widely regarded as the real keeper of the party's purse-strings.
A Paris-region company executive has testified that Casetta effectively controlled access to City of Paris public housing contracts in exchange for cash payments.
Justice sources said she worked closely with Jean-Claude Mery, a Paris consultant who is under investigation for alleged large-scale illicit fundraising on behalf of the Gaullist party.

Police are also conducting a preliminary investigation into allegations that Casetta received a fictitious 25,000 francs ($5,000) monthly salary from a subsidiary of public works giant Compagnie Generale des Eaux in 1991-94.
Her lawyer was not available for comment on the cases.
